reviews.title: I no longer trust Amazon with my personal data.
reviews.text:
I no longer trust Amazon with my personal data.

After what happened with my Amazon account, I have made the decision to remove all of my private photographs from Amazon Photos.

My account was compromised and, following this, I became the victim of a scam in which I lost almost £700. I have provided Amazon with evidence of what happened, yet they continue to deny that there was unauthorised activity and I have not received the support or reassurance I would expect after something this serious.

What concerns me now goes far beyond the money.

Amazon Photos contains years of private and personal photographs. After losing confidence in the security of my account, I simply do not feel safe leaving them there. One of the most disturbing thoughts is not knowing whether the people who gained access to my account may also have been able to access my photographs.

I sincerely hope they did not. But the fact that I am even having to worry about this says everything about how this experience has affected my trust in Amazon.

I have been a loyal Amazon customer for years. Perhaps one individual customer means very little to a company with millions of customers, but behind every account is a real person, with private information, memories and a reasonable expectation that their data will be protected, and that they will be taken seriously when something goes wrong.

Instead, I have been left feeling unsupported, dismissed and deeply insecure about what information may have been exposed.

reviews.title: Doesn’t navigate back anymore
reviews.text: When using the mobile app to organize albums, using the search bar to find a specific prefix (e.g., searching "Vacation") brings up the right folders. However, when I tap on an album and then press "Back," the app completely wipes out my search query and resets to the main folder root instead of keeping me on my active search results.Please make the search results "stateful" so the app remembers my search query when I press back. The current behavior makes managing large, prefix-based album structures very frustrating.

reviews.title: Warning to RAW file users
reviews.text:
RAW data is completely lost when backing up. Files still
upload in a raw container but contain only a JPEG.

E.g. I upload a 25 MB ProRaw .dng file on the app. The file is still a .dng if you download it from amazon photos website but only 2 MB. All the raw data is missing.

This seems to happen with any raw file - same thing happens with .cr2s from photos I imported from a canon.

Please fix this! There is no such issue on the android version of the app

reviews.title: Horrible to use
reviews.text:
The app is really badly designed. Photos and videos only back up if the app is open and visible. It doesn’t run in the background so you have to remember to leave it running every night to upload any photos taken. 
The usability once uploaded is ok but could be improved greatly. It’s not a patch on the Apple photo storage and functionality. 
It works as a back up only but is awful if you’re looking to use it instead of the native photo storage. 
No AI function added. No advanced folder options. No search function. 
The selection multiple is not great either. Overall as a safety net it’s passable at best.
